lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: roommates, shared costs, and written agreements

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic roommates, shared costs, and written agreements task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner sits down with a guardian and, using a provided list of topics that shared-living agreements commonly address (how rent and shared costs are split, how chores and cleaning are handled, what happens if someone needs to move out early, and a policy for guests staying over), talks through each topic as a hypothetical: if the learner were sharing a place with a roommate someday, what would a fair, specific, written answer to each topic look like?
safetyNotes: This is a planning conversation about a hypothetical future roommate situation; no real roommate, lease, or shared housing arrangement is created or signed.

The learner shares only as much about household finances or preferences as they and their guardian are comfortable discussing; no specific real dollar amounts need to be disclosed to complete the lesson.

simulationAlternative.description: If a guardian is not available for a live conversation right now, the learner instead reads a provided sample dialogue between two roommates discussing these same topics, writes what they would add, change, or ask differently if it were their own conversation, and reviews that written work with a guardian afterward for sign-off.

materials: learner-local: the provided list of common roommate-agreement topics

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What part of this conversation would you have been most likely to skip if you were doing it for real without practicing first, and why would skipping it be risky?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Topic coverage: All four topics were discussed and appear, in some form, in the task 3 list. | Concreteness of agreement items: At least four of the five to six items name a specific, workable mechanism. | Reflection on the value of practicing: Reflection names a specific part that would have been skipped and a plausible reason why. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draft the actual one-page written agreement based on the finalized list, in a form they could adapt later for a real roommate situation.

resources.title: roommates, shared costs, and written agreements coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner sits down with a guardian and, using a provided list of topics that shared-living agreements commonly address (how rent and shared costs are split, how chores and cleaning are handled, what happens if someone needs to move out early, and a policy for guests staying over), talks through each topic as a hypothetical: if the learner were sharing a place with a roommate someday, what would a fair, specific, written answer to each topic look like?
Coach direction: Before the conversation, name a conflict a written agreement might have prevented.
Learner prompt: Name one shared-living conflict you've heard about (from a book, show, or someone you know) that a written agreement might have prevented.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: roommates, shared costs, and written agreements complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your guardian, talk through each of the four listed topics as a hypothetical.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I discussed with my guardian how rent and shared costs would be split.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I discussed how chores and cleaning would be handled.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I discussed what would happen if a roommate needed to move out early.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I discussed a policy for guests staying over.

Equal-access rule: If a guardian is not available for a live conversation right now, the learner instead reads a provided sample dialogue between two roommates discussing these same topics, writes what they would add, change, or ask differently if it were their own conversation, and reviews that written work with a guardian afterward for sign-off.

resources.title: roommates, shared costs, and written agreements minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What part of this conversation would you have been most likely to skip if you were doing it for real without practicing first, and why would skipping it be risky?

Success checks: Topic coverage: All four topics were discussed and appear, in some form, in the task 3 list. | Concreteness of agreement items: At least four of the five to six items name a specific, workable mechanism. | Reflection on the value of practicing: Reflection names a specific part that would have been skipped and a plausible reason why.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: roommates, shared costs, and written agreements supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional roommates, shared costs, and written agreements condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Topic coverage: All four topics were discussed and appear, in some form, in the task 3 list. | Concreteness of agreement items: At least four of the five to six items name a specific, workable mechanism. | Reflection on the value of practicing: Reflection names a specific part that would have been skipped and a plausible reason why..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
